images.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: editorial cartoon for an English technical blog about AI agent confusion matrices. Create a horizontal hand-drawn ink and light watercolor cartoon on warm ivory paper, restrained navy, muted sage, faded coral. Scene: hospital reception. An adult patient on crutches with a large clearly visible leg cast, fully clothed, looks incredulous at a friendly small robot acting as a triage assistant behind a desk. The robot cheerfully points to a green check mark on its screen. One speech bubble from the robot says EXACTLY "You are perfectly healthy!" The patient is clearly injured but no gore, distress, mockery of disability, or invasive treatment. The joke is the robot's mistaken classification. Clean editorial linework, gently humorous, lots of whitespace, legible bubble, no other text, no logos, no watermark. Wide composition about 3:2.

editorial_review: Accuracy includes both TP and TN, not just correctly identified positives.
Recall uses actual positives (TP + FN); precision uses predicted positives (TP + FP).
FPR is FP / (FP + TN); it is not the fraction of recommendations that are wrong.
The confusion matrix has four outcomes, not four statistical hypotheses.
ROC plots TPR against FPR across thresholds. AUC summarizes the score ranking and is fixed when only the threshold changes.
Email interest does not grant permission. The relevance matrix evaluates the already eligible pool; an execution-time permission gate blocks opt-outs.
A cast is a cartoon illustration, not proof of a need for ward admission. Illness, admission eligibility and surgery eligibility require different labels.
Investment suitability is defined from decision-time criteria, not retrospective profit. Execution and financial outcomes are evaluated separately.
An LLM's self-reported confidence is not automatically a calibrated probability.
Unknown labels remain unknown. An unsent offer or unreviewed rejected case cannot automatically be treated as negative.
Logs enable an evaluated improvement process; logging alone does not cause a model to learn.
